insights: Distributed traces show repeated gRPC UNAVAILABLE errors (grpc status code 14) affecting frontend-proxy requests — get_traces returned 20 error traces all with error_message '14 UNAVAILABLE'.

Root cause identified: the Ad backend (service 'ad', oteldemo.AdService/GetAds) returned rpc.grpc.status_code=14 and logged 'UNAVAILABLE' exceptions for GetAds calls; these failures propagated back through frontend and were observed by frontend-proxy.
Envoy/frontend-proxy surfaced these upstream gRPC failures as HTTP 500 responses to clients (spans show http.status_code=500 and otel.status_code=ERROR).

Trace-level upstream attributes identify the network target(s): Envoy egress spans show upstream_cluster='frontend' and upstream_address='10.96.158.82:8080', while ad server spans report server.address='ad' and server.port=8080 — allowing direct mapping of failing calls to the ad backend.

Example correlation artifact: traceID 65702bee838d92411cde93834f6a2c7d includes x-request-id=e5c198df-62a2-9897-b2cf-e8f12286149c, timestamps and exception stacktrace containing '14 UNAVAILABLE', suitable for timeline/debugging.
Frontend-proxy logs (stdout) did not include the textual UNAVAILABLE/gRPC error lines; tracing was required to locate the true origin of the failures.

Dependency chain observed in traces (examples): frontend-web -> frontend-proxy -> frontend -> ad (ad is the final failing dependency), indicating the failure occurs in the ad service call path invoked by frontend.

Confirmed hypotheses: UNAVAILABLE errors originate from the ad gRPC backend and cause the HTTP 500s at frontend-proxy. Disproved hypothesis: that Envoy logs would contain the UNAVAILABLE entries (they did not).
